hub.t1.title: T1 · Tools
hub.t1.grab: Take a tool from the wall (grip button or G)
hub.t1.holster: Put it on your belt: B/Y button (or H). Dropping it next to the green ring at your hip also works
hub.t1.drop: Let go of it away from you: it falls to the floor
hub.t1.recover: Pick it up from the floor (it returns to the wall by itself in 10 s). To take it off the belt: B/Y with an empty hand
hub.toolwall.hint: Grip (G): take · B/Y (H): belt · carry it to repair

hub.sources.use.donki_recent: Space weather: LIVE from api.nasa.gov when online; otherwise this record → The Sun now (Crew quarters)

hub.elec.title: ELECTRONICS BENCH · RECEIVER POWER SUPPLY
hub.elec.scope.title: OSCILLOSCOPE
hub.elec.scope.values: Voltage: peak {vpk} V · ripple {vpp} Vpp · final output {vout} V
hub.elec.quality.ok: ✔ Supply OK: steady 5 V → Telecom receives well
hub.elec.quality.noisy: ⚠ Lots of ripple: the receiver is noisy (signal max {cap} %)
hub.elec.quality.half: ⚠ Half wave: half of the bridge is missing (signal max {cap} %)
hub.elec.quality.brownout: ⚠ Not enough voltage: the receiver barely works (signal max {cap} %)
hub.elec.quality.off: ✖ No output: the fuse blew because of a short circuit (signal {cap} %)
hub.elec.fact.diode: Diode: a one-way electronic valve. Current flows in one direction only. The grey stripe marks the cathode (output) and must match the drawing.
hub.elec.fact.cap: Capacitor: a small reserve that smooths voltage peaks. Mind its polarity (the stripe marks the negative pole −) and its maximum voltage.
hint.elec.guided: Telecom is noisy: the receiver power supply is failing. Take the soldering iron from the tool wall and go to the electronics bench in the central hall: press «Scan».
hint.elec.surge: The storm caused a power surge: a diode in the receiver power supply burned out. Telecom has no signal.
hint.elec.cme: The coronal mass ejection damaged a diode in the receiver power supply.
hint.elec.weak_diode: A diode that was too small overheated and opened: use a 1 A one (1N4007).
hint.elec.cap_swollen: A low-voltage capacitor swelled: the supply voltage was higher than its maximum.
hint.elec.repaired: Receiver power supply repaired: Telecom receives well again.
hub.sources.use.perseverance: Speed (152 m/h), MMRTG generator (≈110 W) and 43 sample tubes of the Perseverance rover → rover console (Control room)
hub.sources.use.rover_photos: Real photos from Ingenuity, HiRISE and Mastcam-Z (backshell, parachute, Séítah, delta) and the latest NavCam → rover NAVCAM (Control room)
hub.sources.use.orbits: Orbits of Earth and Mars (NASA/JPL) → real message delay (Telecom)
hub.sources.use.radlab_sep: Real solar storm of 20/05/2024 measured by Curiosity (RAD) → alert and shelter (Crew quarters)
hub.sources.use.solar_dust: Dust measured by Mars Pathfinder (0.28 % per sol) → solar panels (Power)
hub.sources.use.escenarios_nasa: Three historical scenarios with CME, GST, SEP and flare counts and events → Solar history (Crew quarters)
hub.elec.scope.legend: Yellow: input · Blue: output (smooth = good) · Green: 5 V for the receiver
hub.elec.how.scan: The scanner looks for the broken part on the board
hub.elec.how.scanning: Watch the board: the broken part will turn red
hub.elec.how.remove: Point at the blinking part and pull the trigger to remove it
hub.elec.how.removing: The solder melts and the part comes out
hub.elec.how.insert: Touch the card with the same shape as the green slot
hub.elec.how.inserting: The new part slides into place
hub.elec.how.solder: It is in place but not soldered: touch it to solder it
hub.elec.how.ok: The board is fine. If something breaks, this panel will tell you
hub.elec.msg.part_ok: That part is fine: touch the red one
hub.elec.msg.wrong: That one does not fit: look at the shape of the slot
hub.elec.msg.no_stock: No spares left of that part
hub.elec.info.circuit: How it works: alternating current comes in (~AC), the 4 diodes (D1–D4) turn it into direct current, capacitor C1 smooths the peaks and the regulator gives Telecom a steady 5 V.
hub.elec.info.real: In a real repair each part is measured, the bad one is desoldered and an identical spare is soldered in, the right way round. Here the scanner and the bench do it for you.
hub.spares.subtitle: Parts, filters, sealant and oxygen
hub.spares.inside: WHAT IS INSIDE AND WHAT IT IS FOR
hub.spares.use.spares: Parts to repair breakdowns. Check the status board (west wall).
hub.spares.use.filters: Swap the CO₂ scrubber filter in Power and oxygen.
hub.spares.use.sealant: Seal hull leaks with the sealant gun.
hub.spares.use.o2: Emergency oxygen: opened with the valves in Power and oxygen.
hub.spares.elec_hint: Looking for diodes or capacitors? They are at the electronics bench (west wall).
hub.elec.msg.need_iron: You need the soldering iron: take it from the tool wall (or carry it on your belt)
